I farm 20 mu, and with wheat-maize rotation I will use the same 20 mu for wheat first and then maize after harvest. I have done this for 10 years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked before, then I adjust a little. In our place with well water, I will not save too hard on fertilizer, because if wheat or maize loses yield, that loss is bigger than wasting a bit of fertilizer money. I have middle school education, so I do look at seed, water, and fertilizer together, not only one thing. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the base fertilizer down early, give enough nitrogen, and irrigate about 4 times if the weather is normal. Wheat in our area needs steady management, especially watering at jointing and filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is usually better and most people around me do the same. Maize responds well if fertilizer and water keep up after wheat stubble. Since my farm is 20 mu, I also think about labor and timing. I will use rotary tillage to move fast between crops. On pesticide, I will not spray too many times, but I will not skip key sprays either. I will keep the plan a little on the safe side with fertilizer, because a bad harvest hurts more than spending some extra yuan on inputs.
